families.family_description: OH-rich biopolymer films combined with retained acid or acid-like plasticised phases target flexible, hydrogen-bonded proton pathways in the cold window.
descriptor_match: D2: DES or retained acid can preserve a mobile bound polar phase at low temperature.
D3: starch/chitosan/PVA-type hosts are flexible and hydrogen-bonded rather than brittle inorganic scaffolds.
D4: phosphoric-acid-containing DES motifs support non-crystallising proton-source speciation.
D6: starch, chitosan, and PVA provide dense donor/acceptor functionality for proton relay.
D7: chitosan and low-loaded phosphoric acid strategies indicate conducting-phase retention.

families.family_description: One-dimensional mineral hosts embedded in polymeric matrices can confine hydrated acid networks and guide percolated proton transport while limiting leaching.
descriptor_match: D5: attapulgite and halloysite nanotubes explicitly provide nanoconfinement and channel guidance.
D7: clay-hosted acids are reported to reduce leaching and improve immobilisation.
D4: confined phosphoric acid or acid-containing eutectic phases are plausible non-crystallising proton sources.
D6: phosphoric acid and biopolymer/polyol matrices supply hydrogen-bond relay sites.

families.family_name: Amorphous proton-network solids with hybrid soft domains
families.family_description: Amorphous proton-conducting inorganic networks paired with hydrogen-bonded soft phases aim to suppress disruptive transitions while retaining proton-rich interfaces.
descriptor_match: D1: phosphate glass is an amorphous continuous proton-transport medium.
D6: phosphate glass and phosphoric acid provide dense proton-relay environments.
D7: phosphate networks strongly retain the conducting phase, though stability can be conditional.
D2: added soft polar domains can analogously mitigate low-temperature mobility loss seen for bulk water.

instances.composition_description: A quaternary membrane using chitosan as the acid-interacting biopolymer host, PVA as film-forming polyol, 1D attapulgite as nanoconfining filler, and retained phosphoric acid as proton source.
expected_properties: cold_window: plausible bound-acid/bound-water continuity via OH-rich host plus confined acid
nanoconfinement: 1D clay may guide percolated proton channels
retention: chitosan-clay interactions may reduce acid loss
risk_flags: PA leaching if acid loading is excessive
subzero brittleness depends on plasticisation level
instances.novelty_rationale: The full four-part synergy is not given as an exact composition in the claim pool, but each role is individually supported. It is novel because it merges a biopolymer host, PVA film former, 1D clay nanoconfiner, and phosphoric acid into one cold-oriented architecture.

instances.composition_description: A starch-based membrane plasticised with a choline chloride/phosphoric acid deep eutectic to provide a retained, non-crystallising proton-conducting phase.
expected_properties: D4-like acid state: DES formation may keep the proton source mobile at low temperature
D6-rich network: starch OH groups can support proton relay
cold_window: plasticised polar phase is plausible down to near 200 K
risk_flags: mechanical softness may rise at high DES loading
instances.novelty_rationale: The descriptor pool supports starch as a hydrogen-bonded host and ChCl/PA as a deep-eutectic acid environment, but not this exact merged membrane. The novelty is the direct coupling of a starch channel-forming scaffold with a ChCl/PA proton solvent for subambient operation.

instances.composition_description: A starch matrix containing halloysite nanotubes preloaded or contacted with phosphoric acid to create confined acid-rich transport domains.
expected_properties: nanoconfinement: HNT lumen/surface can localise acid domains
retention: HNTs may suppress phosphoric-acid leaching
D6-rich host: starch contributes dense hydrogen-bonding sites
risk_flags: conductivity may drop if HNT loading blocks continuity
instances.novelty_rationale: Claims separately support starch-based proton channels and PA@HNT retention, but not the exact ternary composite. The novel aspect is using a starch biopolymer to bridge and connect HNT-confined phosphoric-acid domains into a flexible film.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan film blended with a proton-conducting deep eutectic solvent as a plasticised, acid-like conducting phase.
expected_properties: cold_window: DES-like bound polar fluid may remain mobile below room temperature
retention: chitosan can hold high water/DES uptake without disintegration
matrix flexibility: plasticisation should reduce glassy disconnects
risk_flags: DES exudation is possible at high loading
low-temperature data are indirect rather than explicit
instances.novelty_rationale: This is retained as a control because the claim pool directly supports a chitosan/DES blend film with improved proton conduction and structural integrity. It anchors the more speculative cold-side combinations against an evidenced soft-matter baseline.

instances.composition_description: An amorphous phosphate-glass proton network dispersed within a PVA-rich soft film and supplemented with phosphoric acid to create inorganic-organic hybrid relay domains.
expected_properties: pathway continuity: amorphous phosphate glass supports non-crystalline proton pathways
interfacial relay: PVA and PA may form hydrogen-bonded bridges around glass domains
retention: inorganic network may help immobilise the acid-rich phase
risk_flags: phosphate-glass conductivity stability can be conditional
instances.novelty_rationale: The pool supports phosphate glass as an amorphous proton-conducting solid and PVA/PA as hydrogen-bond-capable soft components, but not this exact hybrid. The novelty lies in combining a cold-stable amorphous inorganic pathway with a flexible acid-bearing organic interphase to reduce transition-driven failure.
